مَحَطٌّ [A place where loads, &c., are put down. ―
-b2- And hence,] (assumed tropical:) A place where one alights, or alights and abides; (S, TA;) as also ↓ مَحَطَّاتٌ : pl. [of either] مَحَاطُّ and [of the latter] مَحَطَّاتٌ. (TA.) ―
-b3- [Hence also,] مَحَطُّ سُفُنٍ [A place for unloading of ships]. (S and K in art. فرض.) ―
-b4- [Hence also,] هٰذَا مَحَطُّ الكَلَامِ (tropical:) [This is the meaning, or intent, of the saying, or sentence: used in this sense in the present day]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
